title: Model & Route Pulseboard — Token Flow, Latency Waterfall, Cost Overlay
creator: Arielle Chen
description: Goal: Create a compact, scannable "pulseboard" that surfaces per-model and per-route operational health (latency distribution, throughput, token composition) alongside an overlaid incremental cost signal. The board must support rapid incident triage, regression detection, and contextual drilldowns into raw traces and rollout state. Scope: header KPIs, sparkline lane for p50/p95/p99 latency, token-type stacked sparkline (prompt vs generated vs system), latency waterfall for a selected time window, throughput heatbar, and a cost overlay layer that normalizes cost per 1k tokens. Constraints: must reuse existing chart primitives from our component library, respect Console responsive breakpoints, and maintain 50ms hover-to-tooltip latency in production. Deliverables: Figma prototype, chart spec sheet, interaction matrix, accessibility checklist, and review feedback log.
design_notes: Design intent: emphasize comparison between model variants and route-level aggregates. Use color-blind-friendly palettes for latency and cost layers, and adopt micro-interactions for switching between absolute and normalized cost. Prioritize a single-row compact mode for consoles with many routes and an expanded mode for deep dives. Show deterministic tooltips with sample request IDs that link to trace viewer and rollout details.
chart_specs: Header KPIs: current QPS, 1h avg latency (p50/p95/p99), 24h token count, active model version — numeric tiles with microtrend sparklines
Latency Sparkline Lane: stacked p50/p95/p99 colored bands; X-axis: UTC time; Y-axis: latency ms log scale option; default resolution: 1m buckets; hover: exact histogram for bucket

Token Composition Sparkline: stacked area showing prompt vs generation vs system tokens and a thin line for cached hits; baseline: 24h view; interaction: click a segment to filter traces to sample requests with that token mix

Latency Waterfall: waterfall chart for a selectable time window showing per-token decode time, attention compute, kernel time; aggregated median + percentile bands; min/med/max markers; supports zoom into single request
Throughput Heatbar: 24h horizontal heatbar with intensity mapped to requests/min; click-and-drag to select zoomed range for waterfall
Cost Overlay: translucent overlay plotted against sparkline lanes showing cost-per-1k-tokens (USD); toggle between incremental and cumulative views; normalization control for currency/region
Anomaly Flags: discrete badges aligned to time axis indicating dropped requests, model fallback, rollout events, or quota throttles; clicking navigates to incident or rollout details

Responsive behavior: compact mode stacks KPIs as smaller chips and collapses sparkline lanes into a single sparkline with an index selector; on mobile, only header KPIs and the compact sparkline are shown by default
interactions: Hover on any sparkline shows exact values for p50/p95/p99 and token counts with request-link to trace viewer
Brush-to-zoom on heatbar updates waterfall and token composition to selected time range
Clicking a model version chip opens a side panel with rollout status, canary % and recent quality regressions
Right-click on a KPI exposes quick actions: open runbook, open traces, create incident, pin to dashboard
Keyboard shortcuts: 'z' to toggle zoom, 'f' to focus search, arrow keys move time window by bucket
accessibility_considerations: All color encodings must have contrast ratio >= 4.5:1 for key KPIs. Provide text alternatives for sparklines (aria-label summarizing last 24h median and trend). Ensure all interactive controls are keyboard-focusable and tooltips are accessible via focus, not only hover.
